content:
Apple has outlined plans to allow users to copy and paste content between iPhones and Windows PCs, in response to Microsoft's interoperability request in the EU. Details below.

Feature may be EU-only

As discovered by MacRumors, Apple has added a new entry to its "EU Interoperability Requests" page, showing the company has agreed to develop a solution that will allow extensions to share and import iPhone clipboard items with paired devices, including Windows PCs.

In Microsoft's original request, received on March 25, 2026, the company said it is currently unable to offer an experience comparable to the "Universal Clipboard" feature, which lets users copy and paste content between Apple devices.

Microsoft further requested persistent clipboard access so that clipboard syncing between iPhone and Windows PCs can be ongoing, and listed three main use cases:

Copying text or other supported content on iPhone and pasting it directly into a Windows PC, and vice versa. Performing common productivity workflows without needing to bring an app to the foreground or repeatedly performing manual actions to initiate a transfer. The clipboard sync experience as a lightweight, persistent capability rather than a manual, app-driven operation.

The company noted that "copy and paste across devices is a fundamental productivity interaction that users expect to 'just work' between their primary devices," and added that its intent is "not to replace or replicate Apple's system experience, but to enable the basic cross-device productivity users already expect when working across devices."

Apple subsequently responded on April 27, saying that after an initial assessment of Microsoft's request, it has decided to "move it to the next stage of our interoperability process."

Then, on June 26, Apple confirmed it would develop a solution and outlined how the anticipated feature will work.

Apple's update is as follows:

The company also explained that Microsoft will need to rely on AccessorySetupKit, a framework that recently also drew criticism from Meta, which in its own EU interoperability request wants to support AirPods-like pairing between an iPhone and iPad.

In Microsoft's case, AccessorySetupKit will be used to obtain permission to share clipboard contents with paired Windows PCs, with the user needing to authorise once per device.

Apple described the project as "a significant engineering effort" and said it plans to complete development in autumn 2027, shortly after which it will release the solution in a developer beta before a full public rollout.

This timeline suggests the feature could ship as part of iOS 28, although Apple has not confirmed which software version it will be included in.
